messages:
Anika: heads up — starting bring-up for marlin-7b (mistral-style checkpoint) on the Llama runtime, seeing weird token boundary artifacts in generation.
Matt: what do you mean by artifacts? samples or logits?
Anika: short samples — repeated partial token fragments near punctuation, more obvious with long prompts. looks like a vocab boundary + rotary phase mismatch.
Sasha: can you paste a minimal reproducer?
Anika: sure — repro prompt: 'In 2040, cities will' -> output: 'In 2040, cir/ty will' (slash indicates mid-token break).
Jamie: hmm. could be tokenizer mapping off-by-one during conversion. did you run the vocab remap tool with --preserve-sentinels?
Anika: yes. used remapper v2, but we had to apply a custom merge for rare tokens. suspect mapping moved some byte-fallthrough tokens.
Matt: also check rotary params: marlin was exported with headwise rotary frequency scaling (freq_scale != 1). our Llama runtime assumes uniform base freq table.
Sasha: good call. if k/v cache indexing and rotary angle alignment are off by even one index, it looks like mid-token artifacts.
Anika: ran quick hypothesis test: 1) swapped to using the model's original rotary table vs our generated one, 2) patched tokenizer to preserve old eos index. result: artifacts reduced but not gone.
Jamie: can you share the conversion command you ran?
Anika: conversion snippet:```bash
convert-checkpoint --src-format=mistral --dst-format=llama --vocab-remap remap-v2.json \
  --rotary-table marlin_rotary.npy --preserve-eos
```
Matt: try also toggling headwise vs global rotary application. our runtime has a headwise fallback flag: `--rotary-headwise=true|false`.
Sasha: also dump the first 8 token ids for your prompt before and after remapping. that will confirm if any tokens split.
Anika: dump below:
original ids: [320, 4096, 12, 98, 40599]
remapped ids: [320, 4096, 12, 98, 1003]
Matt: there — 40599 -> 1003 is suspicious. looks like a merged rare token got mapped to a common subtoken. that would produce mid-token splits.
Jamie: does the tokenizer normalization (NFKC) change anything? marlin's tokenizer was NFD historically.
Anika: we tested NFKC vs NFD -> NFD matches the training data better, reduces split cases.
Sasha: hypothesis: two issues compounding: vocab remap collapsed rare-to-common mapping + rotary table index offset by one for long context (cache warmup). either alone noisy, together produces slash-like mid-token break.
rotary-bot: CI job queued: rotary-index-sanity-check #8791 (ETA 12m) :gear:
ml-ci: added smoke test: `samples/long_prompt_vocab_probe.py` to reproduce locally.
Matt: next steps: (1) revert that specific remap entry (40599) to original token, (2) test with `--rotary-headwise=true` and `--rotary-index-offset=0/1` grid, (3) run longcontext smoke + unit tests.
Anika: on it. will push a small conversion patch and results in this thread.
Sasha: if still failing after that, capture kvcache dump (first 16 positions) and we'll scan for phase drift.
Anika: thanks — sending PR in a few. :thumbsup:
Matt: nice. if we get a clean repro, we should add an automated conversion lint to flag remaps where rare token -> common token mapping occurs.
Jamie: agreed. prevents regressions when custom merges are used.
Anika: PR linked: https://git.redwood/marlin-conversions/pull/42 (contains conversion diff + sample outputs)
ml-ci: rotary-index-sanity-check #8791 completed: 1 failed, 3 passed. failing case = offset=1 grid.
Anika: patch: reverted remap entry and forced NFD tokenizer; re-run -> artifacts gone on local. pushing to CI now.
Sasha: great — once CI is green let's document recommended conversion flags in the onboarding checklist.
Anika: will add to docs: `eng-ml/onboarding/marlin` (short checklist).
Matt: solid. thanks team.
